text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT alert — multiple GPU OOMs detected in prod-decode-pool (avg 3.2 OOMs/min) · PD alerted :rotating_light:

maya: saw the alert, oncall taking it. what service? any customer impact yet?

zane: looks like streaming decode nodes (decode-v3) starting to crash/restart. K8s shows repeated OOMKilled on container runtime. Some 502s reported by gateway.

anya: pulling logs now — appears correlated with very long sequences, KV cache growth spike. low signal from normal token distributions.

kevin: running quick query on traces, traffic spike from one client id (client_id=acct_8XJ). They've been sending generation requests with unspecified max_tokens in recent SDK change. gateway used to inject default but a rollout removed that default in the proxy.

julie-cs: customer-success here — which customers impacted? we already have 2 tickets opened complaining about dropped responses. want to bubble to them.

luca-ops: copying commands I ran:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n prod-decode -l app=decode-v3 -o wide
# pod decode-v3-72f9  OOMKilled  restartCount=5
kubectl logs decode-v3-72f9 -c runner | tail -n 200
```
logs show repeated allocation failure in cudaMalloc followed by out-of-memory in decode loop. stack trace points to kv_cache.grow path.

maya: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) re-enable default max_tokens admission at gateway (hard cap 2048) 2) apply temporary rate-limit for the offending client 3) cordon a subset of decode nodes and drain 4) fallback route to cpu-fallback group for non-latency-critical requests.

infra-bot: quick note — autoscaler already at target, adding nodes will not help if single-request allocation > gpu mem.

zane: confirmed — single request attempted ~1.8M tokens due to missing max_tokens header + client sending streaming with no stop. KV cache grew linearly per token and exhausted GPU memory.

anya: reproducer from logs:
```json
{"request_id":"r-8abc","stream":true,"prompt_len":256,"max_tokens":null}
```
client SDK previously defaulted to 512 but new build omits header. proxy rollout that removed default means nodes interpret as unbounded.

kevin: timeline: proxy change rolled out ~09:12 UTC, OOMs first spike ~09:18 UTC. correlation looks strong.

maya: actions in progress:
- @zane applying IP-level rate limit on acct_8XJ (block further large streams)
- @anya patching gateway to inject default max_tokens=512 for requests missing header (hotfix)
- @luca-ops cordoning 3 worst nodes and draining streaming pods off them to prevent repeated restarts
- @kevin preparing a rollback of the proxy change if hotfix doesn't hold

luca-ops: running drain: `kubectl drain decode-v3-72f9 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — node evictions started.

infra-bot: mitigation applied: gateway hotfix to inject max_tokens=512 pushed to prod-proxy canary (10% traffic) — monitor for OOM counts.

maya: monitoring dashboard: OOMs dropped from 3.2/min to 0.4/min after canary hotfix, but still some residual errors (client retry loops causing bursts).

julie-cs: telling impacted customers: initial message sent to two accounts reporting drops; said we're mitigating, ETA unknown. will update at 30-min cadence.

zane: found one more nuance — some SDK clients set max_tokens very high intentionally for long-form workflows; hotfix will cap at 1024 by default, but we need an operational path for customers that legitimately need >1024 tokens (account-level opt-in).

kevin: proposed permanent fixes:
- reintroduce enforced max_tokens cap at gateway with configurable per-account overrides
- fail-fast on requests that request > gpu-remaining threshold (return 413 or 429) rather than attempting allocation
- telemetry alert when KV cache growth rate exceeds threshold per-request

maya: short-term rollback staged if hotfix fails. kevin go ahead with rollback plan at +15 if OOMs don't reduce.

luca-ops: status update 09:47 UTC — rolled hotfix to 100% traffic; OOMs reduced to baseline and node restarts subsided. draining completed on three nodes, they came back stable after moving pods.

anya: uploaded snippets to incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incident/3290004444 (internal) — includes logs, sample offending requests, and the patch diff.

julie-cs: CS update: two customers had partial request drops and got 502; both are on trial accounts running experimental SDK. No revenue-tier customers impacted. I'm following up with detailed incident note and apology.

zane: postmortem notes for triage:
- root cause: proxy rollout removed default max_tokens -> allowed unbounded streaming -> KV cache growth -> GPU OOM on decode nodes.
- contributing factor: lack of fail-fast admission with clear error to client and missing per-request KV growth telemetry.

maya: oncall handoff in 30m; leaving follow-ups for postmortem owners (@kevin for proxy change, @anya for gateway caps, @luca-ops for node draining runbook).

oncall-bot: Handoff scheduled: maya -> zane at 10:15 UTC. Please acknowledge.

zane: acked, will take postmortem and runbook updates.

julie-cs: will publish customer-facing summary after engineering confirms final root cause and fix plan.

maya: closing note — watch for any regressions from hotfix (esp customers who legitimately need >1024 tokens). we'll implement per-account opt-ins and better telemetry before removing the cap. :white_check_mark:
